To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
leptin is present in the rat prostate and its release is modulated by androgens, and it is likely that it is involved in prostate functional regulation.

1) leptin and its receptor are expressed in rat seminal vesicles (SV) and prostate; 2) the highest expression of the Ob-Rb and the lowest expression of the Ob-Re isoform were in SV and lateral prostate lobo, respectively; 3) leptin increased acid phosphatase (AP) release from SV and decreased it from the Coagulating lobe of the prostate.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the possible functional role of leptin/obesity-related genes in the prostate, a gland that is not considered to be a classical site of leptin action, but which may be of importance in the development and progression of benign and malignant prostate diseases.
the expression and regulation of leptin in the male reproductive tract and its effects on prostatic acid phosphate secretion.
the expression of leptins and leptin receptors in the prostate, and their possible role in the regulation of prostate function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

leptin is a paracrine regulator in rat seminal vesicles, but an autocrine regulator in the coagulating prostate lobe, and that the lateral lobe is a mixed gland, in which the paracrine and autocrine effects of leptin are balanced.

, although leptin is expressed and the leptin receptor is present in the prostate and seminal vesicles, it is not yet clear if the expression of leptins and their receptors is a mere coincidence, or if they play a role in the physiology and pathophysiology of the prostate.
the expression of leptins and leptin receptors in the prostate may be involved in autocrine and/or paracrine regulation of prostatic functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the leptin system is involved in the regulation of seminal vesicle and prostate function, and that the different components of the prostate may have different roles in this respect.
leptin and Ob-Re may be involved in prostate development and function, and that the different prostate lobules may have distinct functional roles in this respect.
the leptin and its receptor are expressed in the rat prostate and seminal vesicles and leptin may be a paracrine/autocrine regulator of these organs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prostate is a potential target of leptin, which may be involved in its autocrine-paracine regulation.
leptin may play a key role in the functional regulation of the male reproductive system.
leptin and its receptors are expressed in the prostate, and leptin has functional effects on the prostate.
